endorsements.quote: AI should be viewed as a strategic tool supporting, not replacing, physicians.
Targeted educational initiatives and increased awareness of both the potential and limitations of AI are therefore crucial.
In this context, combining AI adoption with lean and change management strategies may facilitate a more effective and sustainable integration into routine clinical practice.

unlisted_practices: Develop and validate KPIs to reliably and reproducibly assess the benefits of AI solutions implemented in clinical practice.
Conduct prospective clinical trials and external validation across diverse populations for AI tools.
Use diverse, multiethnic datasets, perform bias audits and conduct subgroup analyses to mitigate AI bias.
Verify all information gathered through AI by a human.
Base chatbot knowledge on validated sources such as international clinical guidelines with an established source hierarchy.
Equip patient-facing chatbots with automated conversation monitoring and alerts so clinicians can intervene promptly.
Design chatbots to distinguish issues they can manage autonomously from those requiring medical intervention.
Maintain human and economic resources rather than reducing health care personnel alongside AI adoption.
Use interpretable models and explainable AI tools, and document data sources and decision pathways.

screen.reason: This is an expert opinion paper presenting recommendations and frameworks for implementing AI (conversational agents and clinical decision support) alongside lean and change management strategies in breast cancer care.
